title: 12-storey rental tower approved on Dietz Avenue North
subtitle: Green building policy, Uptown BIA levy, home association levies, borrowing limit, surplus land sale and Official Plan changes.
overview: Council approved an Official Plan amendment and zoning change allowing a 12-storey purpose-built rental building at 6 to 14 Dietz Avenue North, replacing the six-storey limit that applied before {{vote:m15}}. The proposal includes some affordable units and family-sized suites. Neighbours raised concerns about height, parking, landscaping and construction impacts, and the Region of Waterloo must still approve the Official Plan amendment.

Council also updated the Green Building Policy for City-owned buildings, banned new natural gas connections, aligned building emissions targets with 50% by 2030 and net-zero by 2050, and asked staff to develop a corporate solar strategy {{vote:m10}}. It released $250,000 for facility transformational projects {{vote:m11}}.

On finances, council set the 2024 Uptown Waterloo BIA levy {{vote:m12}}, approved levies for five home associations, and authorized temporary borrowing of up to $103,339,084 if needed {{vote:m5}}. It declared a Millennium Blvd remnant parcel surplus and approved its sale for $640,000, with proceeds going to the Tax Rate Stabilization Fund {{vote:m14}}. General Official Plan and zoning amendments were also approved {{vote:m16}}.

decisions.detail: Council adopted Official Plan Amendment No. 48 and approved Zoning By-law Amendment Z-23-08 for a 12-storey apartment building at 6, 8, 10, 12 and 14 Dietz Avenue North, and asked the Region to approve the amendment {{vote:m15}}.

Council approved revisions to the Green Building Policy for City-owned buildings, directed updated emissions targets of 50% by 2030 and net-zero by 2050, and asked staff to develop a corporate solar PV strategy {{vote:m10}}.
Council released $250,000 of 2024 non-routine funding from the Climate Action Reserve Fund for the Facility Transformational Projects {{vote:m11}}.

Council declared the remnant parcel surplus and delegated authority to the City Solicitor to sell it to Activa Holdings Inc. at the appraised value of $640,000, with proceeds going to the Tax Rate Stabilization Fund {{vote:m14}}.

decisions.item: General Official Plan and zoning amendments
decisions.detail: Council adopted Official Plan Amendment No. 54 and Zoning By-law Amendment Z-24-01, a set of general updates and clean-ups, and asked the Region to approve the Official Plan amendment {{vote:m16}}.
Council approved the 2024 Uptown Waterloo Business Improvement Area levy of $738,274 and the by-law to impose it {{vote:m12}}.
Council authorized temporary loans, if required, up to an aggregate of $103,339,084 for 2024 to 2026 and directed staff to report back on any borrowing {{vote:m5}}.

Council designated 2024 significant festivals and events for by-law exemption, including Afro Fest, Oktoberfest events, Kultrun, the Royal Medieval Faire, Busker Carnival, Jazz Festival and Wonders of Winter {{vote:m6}}.

debate: Delegates opposed to the Dietz Avenue development raised concerns about the 12-storey height, reduced parking, reduced landscaping and setbacks, and sunlight and privacy for neighbouring seniors' apartments. One delegate disputed the parking and shadow studies.

Supporters, mostly renters, said the city needs purpose-built rental housing, including two- and three-bedroom units and affordable units close to transit. They said the site is in a major transit station area and that building up helps protect farmland.

One delegate asked that the affordable units be secured for the life of the building and that a master plan be completed for nearby lands. Staff said current planning law gives the city no tool to require long-term affordability, and that the Official Plan review will set the broader framework.
Staff said the City's bedrooms-per-hectare density rule tends to favour one-bedroom units, which is why they supported a higher density here.

On the Green Building Policy, councillors asked about short-payback measures and the case for early equipment replacement. Staff said heat pumps added to gas boilers are the main route to the 2030 target, with solar adding smaller savings.
